title: POC scoping: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private - Orion Telecom
next_steps: Sam to send draft POC proposal and pricing tiers for Hosted vs Dedicated by 2026-10-06
Priya to share benchmark plan and test dataset guidance by 2026-10-05
Orion team (Mark) to provide 2 weeks of traffic profile and sample prompts by 2026-10-07
Schedule a bench run (end-to-end) for week of 2026-10-12, Priya to propose exact slot
action_items: Sam Taylor: draft POC scope & pricing; due 2026-10-06
Priya Desai: benchmark plan + test harness; due 2026-10-05
Mark Jensen: traffic profile and retention constraints; due 2026-10-07
Leah Ortiz: security questionnaire answers (SOC2 logos, KMS requirements); due 2026-10-08
summary: AE/SE kickoff to scope POC across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployment options. Focus on success criteria (latency 95th pct target, cost per 1M tokens, data residency), workload sizing, benchmark plan and timeline for a 3-week POC leading into pilot. Security constraints (KMS, SSO, audit logs) push towards Dedicated/Private for sensitive traffic; Hosted considered if data can be token-masked and retention accepted.
topics: Success criteria: latency SLOs, throughput, cost targets, quality/regression thresholds
Workload sizing: peak qps, avg tokens per request, embedding batch sizes
Benchmarks: synthetic vs production replay, metrics to capture (p95 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization)
Deployment decision criteria: data residency, compliance, predictable throughput, cost tradeoffs
Timeline and next steps for a 3-week POC
transcript:
[00:00] Sam (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick intros - I'm Sam Taylor, account exec for Redwood.
[00:08] Mark (Orion): hi, Mark Jensen here, VP Eng, Leah on security, Amit on SRE.
[00:15] Priya (SE): Priya Desai, I'll lead the benchmarking and technical scoping side.
[00:22] Mark: great, we're looking to evaluate a POC to replace our internal intent-classifier and some routing logic, goal is sub-200ms p95 on 128-token prompts and about 20k qps for the combined service during peak windows, and of course cost is a big driver.
[00:40] Sam: thanks Mark, super helpful. quick clarifying q: is that 20k qps for single model or across multiple endpoints?
[00:46] Mark: across the platform, multiple routes - think 3 model endpoints, average request is 80-150 tokens, embeddings for search will be batched separately.
[00:56] Leah: also to flag compliance: we need SOC2, must manage keys via our KMS, and audit logs retained for 1 year. some traffic must never leave the EU; data residency is a hard req.
[01:10] Priya: that pushes us toward Dedicated or Private for those EU-bound flows, but we can still consider Hosted for non-sensitive traffic if masking works.
[01:18] Amit: can you explain how Redwood Dedicated differs from Redwood Private again? we're not totally clear on the boundaries.
[01:25] Sam: sure, short version: Hosted is our multi-tenant public API — fastest to stand up and lowest ops friction. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools just for you in our cloud tenancy — predictable throughput and isolation, with contractual SLAs. Private is customer-managed control plane/VPC or on-prem option for fully isolated deployments and direct KMS/HSM integrations.
[01:47] Mark: ok, cost-wise we're guessing Dedicated is expensive but better performance, Private probably even pricier because of infra. is that fair?
[01:55] Priya: yes and no — Dedicated gives you most of the performance benefit with lower engineering lift vs Private. Private comes with extra infra and ops work but is needed when you have strict residency and key material controls. quantization and batching strategies can impact GPU counts too.
[02:10] Sam: for the POC we usually recommend a 3-week scoped test: week1 instrument and replay traffic + small smoke tests; week2 run microsbenchmarks and initial scale tests; week3 full-scale run and results + decision workshop.
[02:23] Mark: sounds good. what metrics will you capture?
[02:26] Priya: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, GPU utilization, cache hit rates (prefix/KV cache), error rates and output quality — we can run a side-by-side quality eval set to detect regressions.
[02:40] Leah: about audit and keys — can Hosted satisfy our KMS requirement if we manage keys?
[02:45] Sam: Hosted doesn't allow customer-managed keys today; Dedicated supports bring-your-own-key via KMS integration in our tenancy, and Private obviously can integrate directly with your on-prem KMS or cloud KMS inside VPC.
[02:58] Amit: ok. for throughput estimation, what kind of GPU counts should we expect per 1000 qps for a 128-token average using a quantized 7B model?
[03:06] Priya: rough ballpark: with q4_8 or similar quantization and batching you might push 800-1200 qps per A100-equivalent GPU with optimized kernels, but model choice and prompt size swings that. for a 13B model expect significantly lower qps. we'll run real replays to size properly.
[03:23] Mark: good — so initial bench will tell us how many GPUs and which model variant to pick.
[03:27] Sam: and cost tradeoffs — we can show cost per 1M tokens for Hosted vs Dedicated committed vs Dedicated on-demand, and an estimate for Private including infra plus support.
[03:36] Mark: what about failover? if Dedicated capacity is exhausted do you automatic fallback to hosted?
[03:41] Priya: yes we have smart routing/fallback policies; you can set policy to failover to a lower tier model or to Hosted, preserving availability but with different latency/cost profile.
[03:50] Leah: about logging and PII — can you redact or token-mask at edge? we cannot send raw phone numbers.
[03:57] Sam: you can do client-side token masking or we can set up prefix redaction in the Private flow; Hosted can accept pre-masked payloads. but hosted transcription might still have some metadata we need to guard.
[04:10] Mark: timeline question — how long to stand up a Dedicated POC?
[04:14] Priya: if you go Dedicated in our cloud — about 2-3 business days to provision reserved pools once contracts and capacity are agreed; Private takes longer — typically 2-4 weeks depending on network/VPC peering and KMS configs. Hosted is immediate.
[04:28] Amit: ok can you run a bench with our replay? we have 2 weeks of traffic logs.
[04:33] Priya: yes — please share the logs and a sample of live prompts, we'll sanitize them and run the replay in our bench harness. ideally include traces on request size and inter-arrival distributions.
[04:46] Mark: for success criteria — we want p95 < 200ms for inference on 128-token prompts, cost under $X per 1M tokens (we left that as TBD), and no security red flags. also need to validate quality against current classifier (F1 score not degrade more than 1%).
[05:05] Priya: noted. we'll propose a concrete checklist in the benchmark doc: specific queries, eval harness, acceptance thresholds for latency/cost/quality.
[05:13] Sam: common pitfall to flag — sometimes customers see good synthetic p95 but repro with real traffic shows heavier tails; so we always do a production replay to catch caching, burst behavior and cold KV cache impacts.
[05:26] Mark: makes sense. on routing, we may want low-sensitivity traffic to use Hosted for cost savings and sensitive flows to go Dedicated/Private. is hybrid routing supported?
[05:35] Priya: yes, routing by policy is supported. you can route by customer, region, or route-level flags. we can set canary rules for rollout too.
[05:44] Leah: about audit logs retention — Hosted retains for 30 days by default right? we need 1 year.
[05:50] Sam: default shorter, but Dedicated and Private can extend retention and provide the audit export you need. we also offer log-forwarding to your SIEM in Dedicated/Private.
[05:58] Amit: any legal procurement hurdles for Dedicated?
[06:02] Sam: there's a reserved capacity contract and standard enterprise SLA addendum; procurement can be parallelized with the POC but final Dedicated size and pricing will lock down in the contract.
[06:14] Mark: ok. can you share an example SLO table and typical cost comparison for a 3k qps steady workload?
[06:22] Priya: yes will include that in the POC doc.
[06:25] Mark: what about model drift and regression monitoring?
[06:27] Priya: we recommend a small eval suite that runs every commit and after each model/quantization change; Redwood Optimize can surface regressions and tie alerts to your prompt set.
[06:38] Leah: any certifications for Private deployments? we need to map controls to our vendor questionnaire.
[06:43] Sam: we can share SOC2 reports, ISO certs where available, and a controls matrix. Private deployments let you keep keys and logs in your environment which greatly simplifies the questionnaire.
[06:55] Mark: are there any hidden costs for Private? network egress, peering, ops time?
[07:00] Priya: yes, typically network peering, cross-region bandwidth, and on-prem infra are additional; we'll include a TCO line item for that.
[07:07] Mark: ok last thing — what is success at end of POC? we'll look for verified performance (p95 <200ms), cost model for scale, integration checklist done and security acceptance. if pass, we move to a 3-month pilot on Dedicated or Private.
[07:22] Sam: perfect. next steps recap: Sam sends POC proposal and pricing; Priya sends benchmark plan & harness; Orion shares logs and security questionnaire answers. we'll target bench run week-of 2026-10-12.
[07:36] Mark: thanks all.
[07:38] Sam: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links to POC doc, security deck and benchmark spreadsheet.
[07:45] (call ends)
